title: Ostomy Supply Program Tier Placement and Program Change Rules
content:
An Ostomy Supply Program is opened when Larkfield accepts a referral for this product line, and the tier written on the program is fixed by the coverage the program bills, never by the customer's preference.

## 1. Locating the tier

1.1 The tier is located from the coverage record named on the program: the coverage record's plan type and coverage order must equal the tier's entry gate, and the self-pay tier is used only when no coverage record is named.

| Tier | Entry gate |
|---|---|
| Ostomy Self-Pay Program | No coverage record named; a written order is required |
| Ostomy Commercial HMO Program | Commercial HMO plan, coverage order primary; a network referral is required |
| Ostomy Commercial PPO Program | Commercial PPO plan, coverage order primary |
| Ostomy Medicare Advantage Program | Medicare Advantage plan, coverage order primary |
| Ostomy Original Medicare Program | Medicare Part B, coverage order primary |
| Ostomy Medicaid Program | Medicaid, coverage order primary |

Every tier is open to colostomy, ileostomy and urostomy programs.

1.2 When a customer has two in-effect coverage records, the one whose coverage order is primary fixes the tier, and the secondary coverage only receives crossover or secondary claims. A coverage record whose coverage order is secondary never fixes the tier.

1.3 A customer with an in-effect Original Medicare Part B coverage record cannot be enrolled on the self-pay tier for an item Medicare covers, because Larkfield submits a claim for every Medicare-covered item it supplies to a Medicare beneficiary. That customer is enrolled on the Original Medicare tier, and an item or quantity Medicare will not pay is handled under the program's liability notice rules.

1.4 Any clinical qualification in the tier's entry gate is read from the program's own clinical fields as documented on the prescriber's written order and medical records, never from the customer's description alone.

## 2. Coverage in effect and on file

2.1 The coverage record named on the program must be in effect on the date of the write: its effective date is on or before that date and its termination date is empty or on or after that date. This applies both when a program is opened and when it is changed.

2.2 A coverage the customer reports that is not on file cannot be written onto a program, because coverage records are created only by Larkfield's benefits verification team after the payer confirms eligibility.

| Coverage record on the date of the write (hypothetical dates) | In effect? |
|---|---|
| Effective the same day, no termination date | Yes |
| Effective earlier, terminating on that very day | Yes |
| Effective earlier, terminated the day before | No |
| Effective the day after | No |

## 3. Program changes

3.1 A program change rewrites the coverage reference and the tier together when the customer's insurance changes, and rewrites prescriber or product fields when a newer written order changes them.

3.2 A change never rewrites the program's status.

3.3 After a tier change, the next refill may draw only on an authorization grant recorded under the new tier.

## Basis notes

- *Which record decides the tier?* The coverage record named on the program, read for its plan type and coverage order; the customer's stated preference has no bearing.
- *Can a secondary plan decide the tier?* No; a secondary coverage record never fixes the tier, whatever its plan type.
- Whether prior authorization applies and what coinsurance the customer bears follow from the tier so located, as the tier schedules state them.
